name: Chewing and spitting

lead: Chewing and spitting means chewing food and spitting it out instead of swallowing. In research it is documented as a behaviour in people with eating disorders, such as bulimia.
Published studies are clinical descriptions of patients; none tests it as a way to improve appearance.

paras: Studies describe it as a compensatory behaviour used to avoid calorie intake while experiencing taste, and it has been linked to binge eating.

Papers report it as a marker of greater psychopathology and behavioural severity in inpatients with eating disorders [6]. Anyone affected can seek help from a clinician or an eating-disorder helpline.

lead: Chewing and spitting is a behaviour in which a person chews food for taste and then spits it out without swallowing. In clinical literature it is described as a compensatory or purging-type behaviour seen in people with eating disorders.

In a 1985 study of 275 patients meeting criteria for bulimia, 64.5 percent reported chewing and spitting out food, alongside binge eating (100 percent), self-induced vomiting (88.1 percent) and laxative use (60.6 percent) [1]. Later studies have examined it as a marker of eating-disorder severity [2][3].
infobox: Bulimia nervosa, anorexia nervosa, other eating disorders
Reported prevalence in one 1985 bulimia sample

paras: Peer-reviewed papers have studied the behaviour as a clinical feature of bulimia (1988), among eating-disordered patients (2002), in relation to binge eating (2004), as a compensatory behaviour (2015) and as a marker of psychopathology and behavioural severity in inpatients (2015) [2][3][4][5][6]. It has also been examined in eating behaviour after gastric bypass surgery [7].

Human clinical studies exist, but they are observational descriptions of patients with eating disorders; none tests it as an appearance technique. The 1985 study of 275 patients with bulimia reported its frequency [1].
